Probing Self-Supervised Video Representations — A systematic out-of-distribution study on UCF-101

Date: 2026-05-31 19:01 Model: qubvel-hf/vjepa2-vitl-fpc16-256-ssv2 Dataset: UCF-101 (1059 clips) Hardware: MacBook Pro M5 Max · MPS

Executive Summary

V-JEPA 2’s self-supervised backbone achieves 98.2% linear probe accuracy on UCF-101 — a dataset it was never trained on — while its SSv2 classification head produces confident but semantically wrong predictions for 42% of the same classes. The bottleneck is not the representation. It is the vocabulary.

0.93
Backbone same-class cosine similarity

V-JEPA 2 is a ViT-L (325M parameter) video transformer pre-trained with a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) and fine-tuned for classification on Something-Something v2 (SSv2) — 174 hand-object interaction classes. This project applied the model frozen and zero-shot to UCF-101 (101 action classes it was never trained on), then systematically probed its representations across five phases to understand what its world model actually encodes.

The central finding: the backbone generalises almost perfectly to unseen action categories, achieving 98.2% top-1 accuracy with a simple linear classifier on the frozen embeddings. All four classes the SSv2 head mapped to nonsensical physics primitives (the “blind spots”) achieve 100% linear probe accuracy. The SSv2 classification head — not the backbone — is entirely responsible for the model’s poor zero-shot UCF-101 behaviour.

“The bottleneck is not the representation. It is the vocabulary.”

Phase 2 — Zero-Shot Behaviour Categorisation

1059 UCF-101 videos were run zero-shot through the SSv2 classification head. Each class was categorised by its prediction confidence and label consistency across ~10 videos.

34
HIGH_CONF_CONSISTENT

Model maps confidently to one SSv2 concept across all videos of this class. Often semantically wrong but internally consistent.

25
HIGH_CONF_INCONSISTENT

High confidence but different SSv2 labels across videos of the same class. The backbone sees variation the head cannot resolve consistently.

42
LOW_CONF_SCATTERED

Low confidence, no dominant SSv2 label. SSv2 vocabulary has no good match for these action categories.

Step 3 — Blind Spot Analysis

Four UCF-101 classes cluster in an isolated region of embedding space with no close SSv2 concept neighbours. The SSv2 head cannot assign a semantically meaningful label to these classes.

UCF ClassNearest SSv2 ConceptWhy the Mapping Fails
PoleVaultTurning [something] upside downBody inversion — no SSv2 hand-object contact
WritingOnBoardSprinkling [something] onto [something]Arm arc misread as dispersal / sprinkling
SalsaSpinSpinning [something] so it continues spinningRotation without hand-object contact
SurfingWiping [something] off of [something]Lateral body sweep misread as wiping

Step 3 — “Hitting” Catch-All Absorption

Hitting [something] with [something] absorbed 33 UCF classes. Within-group cosine similarity: 0.6085 vs global baseline 0.93. This label is a spurious catch-all for any repetitive contact motion — not a real semantic cluster.

Step 4 — Hypothesis Testing

Three embedding-geometry proxies were tested against prediction confidence and behaviour category.

Cluster Tightness within_class_similarity +0.153 0.1263 2.961 0.0564 REJECTED
The Tight-Cluster Paradox
21 LOW_CONF_SCATTERED classes have above-median within-class cosine similarity (tight backbone clusters) but low SSv2 confidence. Hypothesis C was rejected — the backbone encodes these classes clearly; the SSv2 head simply has no vocabulary for them. Phase 4 resolves this directly.

Phase 4 — Linear Probe Experiment

A logistic regression classifier was trained on the frozen (1059, 1024) backbone embeddings using 5-fold stratified cross-validation. StandardScaler fit on train folds only. No model reloading — pure sklearn on the cached embeddings.

Tight-Cluster Paradox Resolution

99.5% linear probe accuracy vs 30.8% SSv2 confidence across the 21 paradox classes (delta = +0.687).

Backbone encodes UCF-101 action information for the tight-cluster paradox classes (linear probe 0.995 vs SSv2 confidence 0.308, delta=+0.687). The SSv2 classification head is the bottleneck, not the representation.

Conclusions

  1. The V-JEPA 2 backbone generalises to unseen action categories. Same-class cosine similarity of 0.93 across UCF-101 — a dataset never seen during training — confirms the JEPA pre-training objective produces genuinely general spatiotemporal representations.
  2. The SSv2 classification head vocabulary is the bottleneck, not the representations. A linear probe on frozen embeddings achieves 98.2% on UCF-101. The backbone already has the answer — the SSv2 head simply has no UCF-101 words.
  3. Blind spots are entirely a head problem. PoleVault, SalsaSpin, WritingOnBoard, and Surfing — all flagged as blind spots in Phase 2 — achieve 100% linear probe accuracy. Their embeddings are geometrically clean; the SSv2 vocabulary just maps them to the nearest physics primitive.
  4. SSv2 physics primitives dominate the head’s out-of-distribution vocabulary. “Hitting” (154 clips), “Throwing” (133), “Spinning” (98) absorb the majority of UCF-101 classes because SSv2 was trained on hand-object interactions. Any large motion pattern gets forced into the nearest contact primitive.
  5. Replacing the SSv2 head with a linear mapping would yield ~98% accuracy on UCF-101 with zero backbone training. No fine-tuning, no LoRA, no additional data — just a 1024×101 weight matrix on top of the frozen backbone.

Limitations

  • ~10 videos per class — per-class accuracy is coarse (2 test samples per fold)
  • Linear probe trained and evaluated on the same embedding set used for analysis (no held-out split)
  • Single model (V-JEPA 2 ViT-L SSv2) and single dataset (UCF-101)
  • Class size imbalance in UCF-101 sample (min 9, max 20) introduces minor variance

Future Work

  • Test with other out-of-distribution datasets (Kinetics-400, HMDB-51)
  • Compare LoRA backbone fine-tuning vs head-only replacement on full UCF-101
  • Temporal dynamics analysis using optical flow to validate Hypothesis A proxy
  • Probe intermediate transformer layers to identify where UCF-101 action geometry forms
